summary:
I've written plan.md: a long, low single-storey house of white stucco and dark timber under a pale slab roof that rises only 1.5 blocks over a 10-cell half-span. Its eaves are 2 deep, beam ends stick out past them every 3 cells, and a flat carport roof sits one level lower beside it. The street side is blank apart from a tan ledgestone wall, a clerestory strip and an orange door; the back is floor-to-ceiling glass between dark posts, opening onto a kidney pool. Those layered horizontals, the central atrium and the teal-and-white car on the driveway are what make it read as an Eichler or Palm Springs house. Long white-stucco, dark-timber post-and-beam bungalow: stepped-slab near-flat gable on beam lines every 3, flat carport deck one level lower, blank street face with ledgestone wall and orange door, all-glass garden side, open-sky atrium at the centre.
Open-plan public core (gallery, galley kitchen, dining, living with sunken pit and freestanding fireplace) west of the atrium; corridor with 3 bedrooms and 2 baths east.
Teal/white car, desert front yard, kidney pool and patio behind. 6 parts; elements.md and the plan.md designer sections are written.

house shell and ground: Part 1 shell built in parts/shell.mjs: bedding (dropped by build.mjs), pit floor smooth_quartz at y=0, house floor slab y=1 (terrazzo/spruce/quartz by room), smooth_stone base, white stucco perimeter with OPENINGS left as air, dark_oak_planks header skipping beam lines, atrium ring body air, interior partitions with ROOMS doorways, spruce ceiling y=5 between beams.
make.sh runs clean: shell placed 1848, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE; check shows walkable end to end, and the only floating cells sit under glazing and beams that parts 3 and 4 add. Front-left and back elevation tiles show the shell as planned.
Ticked plan.md part 1 and elements 1, 7, 13, 16 (the spec's ticks); elements 7, 13 and 16 are only partly built here, with glazing and posts left to part 4.
polish: Glazing and posts on the south wall (y=2..4, all of x=10..31 at z=25), the corner posts at (10/31, z=8 and z=25), the clerestory and mullions at z=8, and the atrium ring glass and posts are part 4's; the shell leaves them air.
Part 3 must place the beam logs on the beam lines (y=5, z=5..28) and the roof bands; the header and ceiling cells at y=5 over the air gaps are floating until then.
The bedding at y=-1 is dropped by build.mjs (1122 cells), so it has no effect on build.nbt.
Dirt at y=0 under the house and atrium was already laid by build.mjs before the parts, so the shell does not rewrite it; the pit y=0 is smooth_quartz as specified.
Element 16's y=6 ring glass and the element 7/13 glazing are not built here; the ticks follow the spec's list and the plan.md part boundaries.

waste.what: Worked out each wall segment's cell ranges and doorway/opening skips by hand (north, west, east, partitions, door wall) from plan.md's OPENINGS and ROOMS tables.
waste.cost: about 8 nested loops with hand-computed coordinates; roughly 20 minutes of reasoning-equivalent work in one pass, with one fix (reveal block at x=17 and a duplicate line removed)
waste.tool: A `wall_plan` helper or a plan-to-cells command that takes OPENINGS and ROOMS and emits the air/stucco/header lists per face, so a part only names the stucco and openings, not the loops.

waste.what: Decided by hand which cells later parts own (south glass wall y=2..4, corner posts, clerestory row y=4, atrium ring body, entry niche) and left them as air, since build-only-into-air means shell blocks would block them.
waste.cost: a cell-ownership pass over plan.md's FACADES and OPENINGS sections; no tool output to check it against
waste.tool: A cell-ownership table in plan.md (cell range -> owning part) or a `mcd ownership` check that flags shell cells a later part needs.

waste.what: Checked the floating-block report by eye to tell cells that will be supported later (header and ceiling over the glazed south wall and ring) from real errors.
waste.cost: 18 floating cells in 5 groups reviewed by reading coordinates against plan.md
waste.tool: `mcd check` could tag floating cells that fall under a later part's footprint as pending, not errors.

waste.what: build.mjs writes 1122 bedding cells at y=-1 that the proxy drops and counts; the shell still loops over them because the spec asks for them.
waste.cost: about 1100 no-op set calls per run
waste.tool: build.mjs or the spec could skip below-grid bedding (the grid is 0-based), so the drop count is not noise.

waste.what: Visual check of the shell by rendering and reading tiles, one render call and two images.
waste.cost: 2 images read; no verification by numbers of which cells look like plan
waste.tool: A `mcd render --part` or a per-part cell diff against plan.md's coordinates would have checked placement without reading images.

summary:
site, carport and paving: parts/site.mjs builds the ground layer: sidewalk, driveway with joint rows, sand yard and gravel beds, stepping pads and landing, side strips, back patio, pool deck and lawns (pool cells untouched).
Carport built with vocab carport(floor:true) and breeze_screen(z=21): dark-oak posts/beams, smooth_stone_slab deck, dark fascia, and a checkerboard screen that reads in the front-left tile.
make.sh runs clean: site part 901 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE; mcd check shows no unsupported blocks from this part. Checklist and elements 5, 6, 11, 18, 19, 24 (paving), 25 ticked.
polish: Breeze-screen corner cells at (1,3,21) and (9,3,21) are checkerboard orphans (no post at z=21), flagged by mcd check; kept as drawn, or the screen could start one cell in.

Side-strip conflict: parts list says x=9 z=8..25 sand, but the carport floor (plan VOCABULARY, smooth_stone x=1..9 z=7..21) takes x=9 z=8..21; I followed the floor, so x=9 is sand only at z=22..25 and in the front yard. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
Cacti: saguaro's vocab note says sand under each cactus, but plan.md puts the cluster on the gravel bed; I left gravel. Front part should not add sand, or should confirm.
Element 24 is ticked for paving only; the loungers, patio table and palm (29,31) are part 6's work.

waste.what: Ground-layer rectangles written cell by cell in a nested loop with my own fill/claim helper, because the vocab ground helpers (stepping_pad, joint_row, saguaro sand) only write into air and y=0 is dirt from build.mjs, so they cannot place on the ground layer.
waste.cost: about 10 rectangles and 2 claim rules hand-coded; a retry-free run, but the air-only check made the ground helpers unusable here
waste.tool: A ground-layer helper in vocab (e.g. paveRect(g, x0,x1,z0,z1, block, {free:true}) that writes y=0 over dirt/sand/grass and reports claimed cells), or make the existing stepping_pad/joint_row accept a ground-replace option.

waste.what: Resolved plan conflicts by hand (x=9 sand strip vs carport floor, lawn z=22..25 vs side strips, cacti on gravel vs saguaro's 'sand under each cactus').
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of reading plan.md, elements.md and the parts list side by side
waste.tool: A plan lint that flags overlapping ground rules per cell (parts list vs VOCABULARY vs elements), so the conflict is settled in plan.md before the worker starts.

waste.what: Shell zsh word-splitting: $MCD set to 'node /path/mcd.mjs' fails when used unquoted in zsh, costing a failed check and render call.
waste.cost: one failed command, then a rerun with node called directly
waste.tool: A ready-made mcd wrapper on PATH (a single executable) so workers never build the command string in a variable.

summary:
roofs, beams and fireplace stack: parts/roofs.mjs builds the four stepped slab roof bands with fascia (atrium and chimney rims), dark_oak beam lines on x=10..31 at y=5, gable-end and ring glass at y=6, and the fireplace stack at x=20..21 z=21..22 (lit campfire firebox, black flue, stone cap).
make.sh runs clean: 738 cells placed by this part, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks; build.nbt is whole. mcd check: walkable, no floating blocks; the only orphans are the intended beam ends at z=5 and z=28.
Ticked plan.md part 3 and elements 2, 3, 14. Checked by render only at small size (front-left and back elevation): the roof, chimney and beam tails read; the street-side detail was not closely reviewed.
polish: Chimney flue and the freestanding stack are built but the living-room part (item 27) still owns the shaft's surroundings and the conversation pit; it needs no roof work.
Street-side close view of the roof edge and the chimney cap was not rendered at a zoom that shows detail; check after the merge with the facades part.
vocab fascia_ring rims only one hole; a local chimney-rim loop is in parts/roofs.mjs and noted in plan.md Notes.

waste.what: Chimney-hole rim fascia: vocab fascia_ring takes only one hole, so I wrote a local loop over x=19..22 z=20..23 to swap the flue's roof slabs to dark_oak_slab.
waste.cost: one hand-written loop plus a manual check of which cells are roof slabs (about 4 minutes of reasoning)
waste.tool: fascia_ring should accept a list of holes (or a hole array), so the atrium and chimney rims come from one call

waste.what: Gable-end and ring glass at y=6: I wrote a glazeAir loop per column (x=10, 31 and x=16, 22 over z ranges) by hand.
waste.cost: 4 small loops, coordinates taken from the plan table by hand
waste.tool: vocab glass_bay exists but works on a fixed-x/fixed-z bay with its own y range; a 'glass under band' helper keyed to the ROOF_BANDS table would have removed the coordinate lookup

waste.what: Checking that each roof band had its half and y right: read ROOF_BANDS in vocab/h2 and compared it with the plan's ROOFS table by eye.
waste.cost: one read and a comparison, no build errors
waste.tool: a mcd roof-table check that prints each band's z range, y and half from the plan would make this a single command

waste.what: Reviewing the render: I looked at the iso and back-elevation tiles only, with no close street crop of the chimney and roof edge.
waste.cost: two image reads at small size; the fine chimney detail is not verified
waste.tool: mcd render with a --crop box (x,y,z range) to zoom on one element

summary: facades, glazing and entry: parts/facades.mjs builds the south glass wall (posts on all 8 beam lines, glass y=2..4, slider gaps glazed at y=4 only), the north entry (orange_entry with acacia_door), the clerestory strip, the ledgestone wall with cap, the west/east window bays and the open utility door at (10,2..3,10), and the atrium ring glass and posts. make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt, facades placed 206, no refused or off-palette writes; `mcd check` is clean for my part; y=2/3/4/5 slices match plan.md's coordinates.
polish: Floating spruce_planks at (20..21, 5, 20) and an orphan at (18, 5, 20): the shell's ceiling over the living room sits on air at y=4. Part 1's note assigns the fix to parts 3 and 4; part 3 (beams and roof) should carry this cell, or the living room part should fill it at y=4. Not in part 4's spec, so left as is.
Elements 14 (gable-end glass clerestories at x=10/31, y=6, z=14..19) and the atrium ring's y=6 band glass (x=16 and x=22, z=14..17) are part 3's; not built here.
The west door is set open with hinge=left; if the car or carport needs the swing direction changed, that is a state tweak only.

waste.what: Worked out the south wall bay by bay: which x are beam-line posts, which are slider gaps, and which are glass runs (x=10..31 at z=25), then the atrium ring's glass and door cells on z=11 and z=18.
waste.cost: about 10 min of hand coordinate arithmetic and two rounds of fixing segment boundaries; roughly 20 individual glass and post calls
waste.tool: A vocab helper `glass_wall(g, {x0,x1,z,y0,y1,posts:[beam lines],gaps:[slider x0s]})` or a text layout via layers() on the south wall, so the posts, sliders and glass come from one grid

waste.what: Wrote the utility door by hand (two g.set halves with facing/half/hinge/open states) because no vocab helper covers doors in a wall.
waste.cost: one local helper, about 8 lines
waste.tool: vocab `door_pair(g, x, y0, z, facing, {open})` for any door in a wall (utility door, atrium doors, front door)

waste.what: Checked the result by printing y-slices of build.nbt with a throwaway script (cell map of x=8..33, z=6..26) because the rendered tiles show only the elevation silhouette.
waste.cost: 3 slice runs plus a render; the render alone could not confirm the south glazing or the ring
waste.tool: `mcd slice build.nbt --y 3 --x 8..33 --z 6..26` (an ASCII cell map per y level) would replace the throwaway script

waste.what: make.sh's per-part line reports only g.set refusals, not helper-level skips: vocab h1 returns {placed,skipped} and h3 returns {placed,refused}, so an air-only skip inside a helper is silent in the report.
waste.cost: needed the slice to see that nothing was skipped
waste.tool: Unify the vocab return shape (placed, skipped) and have runParts print the sum of helper skips per part

summary:
car and front garden: parts/front.mjs builds the car_50s (x=3..5, z=1..7), two palms at (12,3) and (30,4), a saguaro, a saguaro, three barrel cacti, two dead bushes and the mailbox at (9,1), 103 blocks, all into air with no refused writes or off-palette ids.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; render shows the car nose-north on the drive, the mailbox, the palms and the cactus cluster in the right places (the front view mirrors x, so the car reads on the right).
Ticked plan.md's checklist for part 5 and elements.md items 20, 21, 22; added a part-5 note to plan.md's Notes.
polish: Cactus ground conflict: plan.md says sand under each cactus, but the site part lays a gravel bed (x=22..30, z=1..5) and cacti only survive on sand or red sand in Minecraft. Part 5 cannot change y=0 (site's blocks are locked). site.mjs needs to put sand at y=0 under the cactus cells (23..29, z=2..4), or the cacti break in game.

The stub site/roofs/facades/back parts are still empty in this copy, so the render shows the car and planting over bare dirt; the final ground and the car's surroundings were not verified against the real site build.
mcd check flags 8 orphan jungle_leaves at palm crown tips (persistent leaves, expected from the vocab palm helper); accepted, not fixed.

waste.what: Worked out the cactus and dead-bush coordinates by hand from the plan's examples and the site table, and checked each against the ground material (gravel bed vs sand) by reading plan.md's site and materials tables.
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of reading and reasoning across plan.md, the site table and the palette
waste.tool: A plan-to-ground query such as `mcd plan ground --at x,z` or a site table keyed by cell that says which material each front-yard cell gets, so a planter can pick cells that are sand.

waste.what: Checked the rendered elevations by eye to confirm placement and orientation; the front view mirrors x (east on the left when viewed from the street), which I had to work out myself.
waste.cost: 3 render tiles opened and reasoned about; one wrong first read of the street view
waste.tool: A render option that labels axes or prints world-coordinate markers for given cells (e.g. `mcd render --mark x,z`), so placement can be confirmed without inferring the mirror.

waste.what: Ticked the checklist in plan.md and the three elements.md items by hand, and wrote the Notes line by hand.
waste.cost: 5 separate edits
waste.tool: `mcd tick <part> --elements <ids>` that updates plan.md's checklist and elements.md items from the built ids.

waste.what: No check that cactus stands on sand. `mcd check` reported no problem for cactus on the gravel/dirt ground, though Minecraft breaks cactus that is not on sand.
waste.cost: found by reading the plan, not by the tool; left unresolved for site.mjs
waste.tool: A `mcd check` rule for surface-dependent blocks (cactus needs sand or red_sand below; dead_bush needs sand, red_sand or terracotta; saplings need dirt-like ground).

summary:
pool, patio and garden details: parts/back.mjs: kidney pool as water at y=0 over the reserved cells with a quartz coping lip at y=1 on the deck; three loungers and a patio table on z=27, a palm at (29,31), four garden lamps (entry (17,5),(21,5); pool (12,29),(23,32)) and two entry lanterns hung under the north header at (18,4,8),(20,4,8). Short grass is seeded on the lawns.
make.sh runs clean: part line shows 109 placed, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks; mcd check reports no problems in this part; the lamps, lanterns, loungers and palm were probed in build.nbt.
Short grass was not verified: my worktree has no site lawn (grass_block), so it placed 0 here; it depends on part 2's lawns landing first.
polish: Pool basin and liner (light_blue_concrete at y=-2 and y=-1) are not built: those cells are below y=0 and not storable. The pool reads as shallow water at y=0 only (elements item 23 left unticked).
Quartz coping is a smooth_quartz_slab lip at y=1 on the deck beside the pool, not the flush coping at y=0 the spec asks for. Part 2 fills those deck cells first, so y=0 would be refused.
No parasol on the patio table (only patio_table with its two chairs). The spec asks for a parasol, but the VOCABULARY says none; elements item 24 left unticked for this reason.

Short grass on the back lawns is coded (seeded, about 35% of open lawn cells over grass_block) but unverified: my worktree has no lawn from part 2, so it placed 0. It needs a check in the merged build.

The palm crown leaves at y=6 are flagged as orphan jungle_leaves by mcd check (touching the build on one face). They are persistent, so they won't decay; the palm is shaped by the vocab helper as written.

waste.what: Checked each back-yard cell by hand with a throwaway probe script (blockAt per coordinate) and printed text maps of y=0/1/2 to confirm the pool, loungers, lamps and palm landed.
waste.cost: about 3 probe/map runs; coordinates for ~12 placements worked out by hand
waste.tool: an `mcd map build.nbt --y 1 --box x0,z0,x1,z1` text view and an `mcd probe build.nbt x,y,z ...` command

waste.what: Expanded the POOL span table into a cell list by hand and wrote my own pool function, because the vocab kidney_pool puts its coping at y=0 on deck cells that the site part fills first.
waste.cost: one rewrite of the pool step; roughly 20 lines of code that a helper would give for free
waste.tool: a kidney_pool option for a raised coping lip (coping='y1') or a pool(cells, coping) helper that takes the deck order into account

waste.what: Looked at the render to see the pool and patio. The back-elevation tile is about 300px and the pool is unreadable, so I checked the layout with text maps instead.
waste.cost: one tile read that showed nothing useful, then the text maps
waste.tool: a top-down (plan) render tile of the back yard, or a --crop/--zoom option on mcd render

waste.what: Resolved a plan conflict myself: PARTS 6 asks for a parasol, but the VOCABULARY says none (the eave is at y=6), and the RESERVED cells don't say where it goes.
waste.cost: a read through plan.md sections, then a decision noted in Notes
waste.tool: a plan detail that gives one answer for the parasol and the coping height

summary:
room: gallery: Gallery part (parts/room-1.mjs): one walkable row z=10 x=16..22 with an orange_carpet runner, a 2-cell birch_slab bench (x=17..18) and three hung lanterns at x=16/19/22 (y=4). make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; room check says OK, 7/7 cells reachable, min light 12, 0 dark.
Render from above reads as a runner, bench and lanterns; the wood-lined walls, coat hook and art are not built.
Lanterns report "nothing above to hang from" in this copy only because the roofs part (beams at y=5 on x=16/19/22) is still a stub here; they should be supported in the merged build.
polish: Wall-hung elements not built: wood-lined north wall (spruce panelling), coat hook wall and item-frame art (item frames are entities, so not blocks); the box is one air row so there is no room for them on the floor.
Lanterns at x=16/19/22 hang from beams at y=5 that the roofs part (parts/roofs.mjs) must place; in this copy that part is a stub, so `mcd check` reports them unsupported until the merge.
Plan checklist items 30 (entry gallery with bench and coat hook wall) and 35 (lit) are only partly met for this room; left unticked.
Gallery is a single 7-cell row, so the furniture is low-profile only (carpet runner, bench, lanterns); no focal piece is placed in the brightest light (brightest cells are the lantern-lit ends, 13).

waste.what: Worked out the gallery's floor cells and walkability by hand from the plan grid: the box is a single row (z=10), so every furniture cell had to be checked against the entrances and the 2-high path rule before drawing.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning, 2 draft layouts discarded (a lantern standing on the floor would block the 1-wide row; a slab under a hung lantern would block head room)
waste.tool: A room-capacity report from `mcd plan --rooms` that lists, per room, which floor cells are free-and-clear-of-entries and which furniture types fit the row (walkable carpets/slabs vs blocking blocks), so one-row rooms are not designed by hand.

waste.what: Room-box spec and plan grid disagree on the corridor opening (spec says x=22, grid wall is at x=23) and on the z=9 row, which the spec text does not describe.
waste.cost: one extra plan query to settle which to trust; used the grid
waste.tool: plan.md room table should give the exact wall/opening cells from the same source the `plan --rooms` grid uses.

waste.what: Wall-hung items (item frame art, coat hooks, wood panelling on the north wall) cannot be built inside this box because the box is air only and the walls belong to the shell; the spec asks for them.
waste.cost: not attempted, decided from the box and the shell lock
waste.tool: A note in plan.md's Notes stating which wall-face cells a room may use for panelling (e.g. trapdoors inside the box), so a designer does not have to guess.

summary: room: kitchen: [\"Kitchen room built in parts/room-2.mjs: galley_kitchen along the north wall (fridge, counter, hob, sink, oven, spruce cabinets), birch-stair stools at a spruce breakfast bar with a potted cactus, an orange_concrete backsplash, and three hung lanterns.\", \"make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt; the kitchen line shows 26 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. `room build.nbt --only kitchen` says OK: 17/17 floor cells reachable, 0 dark, min light 8.\", \"Elements.md item 29 ticked and part 8 added to plan.md's checklist. Room view read: the galley and bar read; the stools read as seats.\"]
polish: The stools are a birch_stairs override over the galley_kitchen helper's birch_slab stools; the helper still writes the slabs first.
Did not view the exterior tiles (front-right etc.); the kitchen sits inside the house, so the room view was the check used.
Floating-block warnings from `mcd check` (y=5 header and ceiling cells around x=14..21, z=18..25) come from other parts, not from the kitchen.

waste.what: Iterated on the layers() import: vocab.mjs does not re-export layers, so the first make.sh failed with a SyntaxError.
waste.cost: 1 failed make.sh run
waste.tool: vocab.mjs re-exporting layers (or a note in the spec naming the build-library import path)

waste.what: Swapped galley_kitchen's birch_slab stools for birch_stairs by a second set() pass over the same cells, because the helper has no stool-block option.
waste.cost: 3 extra set() calls and one rebuild
waste.tool: galley_kitchen option for the stool block (or a stool=stairs argument)

waste.what: Worked out the room's floor-cell layout by hand (fridge, counter, bar, stool and walkway rows) from the room plan text.
waste.cost: about 10 coordinate decisions, plus one off-by-one row fixed after a render
waste.tool: a plan-level furniture-to-cell layout helper that reads a room's free cells and the walkway list

waste.what: Placed the hung lanterns by trial: first set missed the dim cell at (15,2,10), then `room` suggested (11,4,10), which I added.
waste.cost: 1 extra build cycle
waste.tool: `mcd room` lamp suggestions applied automatically, or a lighting plan that puts one lantern per dim cell before the first build

summary:
room: dining: Dining (room-3.mjs): 5x5 box x11..15 z14..18 with a 2x2 spruce-fence table and spruce slab top, six birch-stair chairs (two per side, east column left open as the kitchen-to-living path), a birch sideboard with a potted cactus under the west window, a floor lantern in the SW corner and a pendant lantern over the table at (13,4,15).
make.sh ran clean (dining: 22 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE). `room` check: WALK ok 24/24 reachable, LIGHT min 10, 0 dark. Looked at room.png once; reads as table, chairs and sideboard.
elements.md item 28 ticked; plan.md Notes gained a line on the lantern's beam support and the clear path.
polish: The pendant lantern at (13,4,15) needs the roofs part's beam at (13,5,15). In this copy the roofs stub is empty, so `mcd check` flags it as unsupported. The merged build should be fine; recheck after the merge.
Elements 34 (period furniture) and 35 (every room lit) are not ticked: only the dining furniture is built, and the lit item covers all rooms.

waste.what: Hand-drew the 5x5 dining furniture grid (chair facings, table cells, sideboard, lantern positions) and checked the walk by reasoning about which cells split the room, before running the tool.
waste.cost: about 4 layout iterations in my head, two rewrites of parts/room-3.mjs (the first draft had a multi-character legend key that layers() would not match), about 22 blocks set through layers().
waste.tool: A room-furniture helper that takes a small footprint and a per-side chair count and returns the layers() rows with a through-path check (the `plan --rooms` grid plus a pre-run walk check) would have removed the hand reasoning. vocab dining_set is 4x3 with chairs at both ends, so it would close the room's through path and did not fit this 5x5 box.

waste.what: Read the vocab helpers and build library to learn the stair facing convention and the legend format for layers().
waste.cost: about 4 Bash lookups across vocab/h2.mjs and tools/src/build.mjs.
waste.tool: A one-line note in plan.md or the skill's layers reference: legend keys are single characters, stairs facing = side of the back, lantern hanging needs a block at y+1.

summary: room: living: Built the living room in parts/room-4.mjs: sunken conversation pit with orange carpet rim and coffee table, two orange sofas facing into the pit, egg chair on the north row, sideboard on the west wall, spruce-fence floor lamp, panelling at x=21 z=23..24, three hung lanterns.
polish: Tulip side table (elements 34) not built; the living room has no side table.
Panelling covers only x=21 z=23..24, not the full x=22 partition; the trapdoor facing ('east') is unverified.
The fireplace (x=20..21 z=21..22) is the roofs part's; it is absent in my copy, so the light check ran without the campfire. Re-check the light after the merge.
Hung lanterns at (13,4,23), (16,4,21), (19,4,22) need the beams at y=5 from the roofs part; in my copy they report 'nothing above to hang from'.
The walk check listed 'unreached 12,4,19' (a y=4 coordinate) while the verdict said OK; not investigated.
elements.md item 27 ticked; items 33, 34 and 35 are only partly met by this part (terrazzo and ceiling are the shell's).

waste.what: Worked out by hand which cells each sofa, egg chair and sideboard back and seat cells occupy, so they didn't collide with the pit rim, the doorway lanes and the fireplace footprint. I got this wrong twice before it fit.
waste.cost: About 6 layout iterations on paper, roughly 15 minutes of reasoning.
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for vocab helpers (or `layers`) that reports cell conflicts and blocked walkways against the shell's openings before make.sh runs.

waste.what: Placed the furnished room with per-helper calls instead of one layers() text grid, so I couldn't see the room footprint in text while designing it.
